title: Add Google Cloud to Micetro

cta.text: See Micetro with your own Google Cloud project

prompt:
Product: BlueCat. Demo: "Add Google Cloud to Micetro".
Start with one welcome step whose title is exactly "Add Google Cloud to Micetro" and whose text is exactly: Watch BlueCat Micetro connect to a Google Cloud project, then show its DNS zones and VPC networks beside AWS, Azure and your on-premises servers, and write a new record to Cloud DNS.
Audience: network and DNS engineers and IT leaders evaluating the product. Tone: concise, confident, practical, no hype.
12 screenshots, keep this order, one tooltip per image, calling out the highlighted UI element. Use the text of each numbered tooltip EXACTLY as written; do not rewrite, shorten or merge it. Do not add a closing step or a closing message after the last screenshot; its own tooltip is the end.
1. This is the service list in Micetro. AWS and Azure are already here, next to the DNS and DHCP servers on your own network. Next you add Google Cloud.
2. Google Cloud is a built-in service type, with DNS and IPAM. Choose it.
3. Four details connect a project: a name for the service, the Google Cloud project ID, the email of a service account, and that account's key. The key is masked as you type. The service account needs DNS and network access in the project, and nothing is installed in Google Cloud.
4. The service is added. The banner says the first synchronization can take a few minutes. The new Google Cloud row sits in the list with AWS and Azure, with DNS and IPAM.
5. The project's two Cloud DNS zones are now in Micetro, marked Private, with the Google Cloud service as the authority. They sit in the same list as every other zone.
6. IPAM has the project's network too. The project's VPC networks show under their own Google Cloud account, next to the AWS and Azure accounts: ddi-demo-vpc, plus the default network every Google project starts with.
7. The VPC's two subnets arrive as address ranges, listed with every other network you manage.
8. Now change one of those zones. Open apps.gcp.ddi-legal.net from the list. Its five records are the ones Cloud DNS holds for it, and Create adds another.
9. Create opens the same dialog you use for any DNS zone: a record name, a type, a time-to-live and an address. Nothing here is specific to Google Cloud.
10. Name the record portal and give it the address 10.30.1.20, inside the subnet you just saw. Leave the time-to-live empty for the zone default, then choose Create now.
11. Before anything is written, Micetro asks for a reason. This comment names the change and its ticket, CHG-20419, and it is kept with the change in the zone's history, so anyone can see who changed what, and why. Select Save.
12. Select Save and the record is written to Cloud DNS in your project. The zone now lists six records, including portal, and Google Cloud holds the same record.
